title: Secrets Manager credentials for a ledger service
name: Ledger secrets provider

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code keeps secret values out of places they should not appear? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The ledger database password is rotated in Secrets Manager while the service is running. What happens on the next new connection?
choices: The service keeps using the stale cached password until the process restarts
The first attempt with the cached password may be rejected with InvalidPassword, after which the secret is refetched and one more attempt is made
The service retries forever with the cached password until the TTL expires
boto3 pushes the new value into the provider's cache automatically

questions.prompt: Why is the webhook signature compared with hmac.compare_digest instead of ==?
choices: compare_digest also decodes the hexadecimal string into bytes before comparing
== raises when the strings differ in length, whereas compare_digest does not
compare_digest takes the same time wherever the first mismatching character is, so response timing does not reveal how much of a forged signature was right
compare_digest is required for the str type; == only works on bytes

questions.prompt: Many worker threads call get_json for a secret whose cache entry just expired. What is the behavior of SecretsProvider?
choices: Every thread calls Secrets Manager at once, because the cache check is not synchronized
Threads serialize on one lock, so a single fetch refreshes the entry and the rest reuse it, but all of them wait while that network call runs
Only the first thread waits; the others immediately get the old value
The threads fail with a RuntimeError because boto3 clients cannot be shared
